answers.question: After how many years do I get gratuity?
also: i worked four years will i get gratuity
answers.rendered:
• Gratuity is payable when your employment ends after at least five years of continuous service, including on resignation s. 53(1).
  • You do not need five years if the job ends because of death or disablement, or because a fixed-term contract has ended s. 53(1), second proviso.
  • A fixed-term employee is eligible after at least a year of service under the contract rule 33(1)(a).
  • Gratuity applies to every factory, mine, oilfield, plantation, port and railway company, and to shops and establishments with ten or more employees First Schedule.
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: Am I entitled to a wage slip?
also: employer does not give salary slip
answers.rendered:
• Every employee gets a wage slip s. 50(3).
  • Under the Central Rules it is in Form V, on paper or electronically, on or before payment of wages rule 52.
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: Am I entitled to a weekly day off?
also: ten days in a row without rest
answers.rendered:
• You get rest for one day every week, usually Sunday if you work six days a week Wages Rules rule 6(1).
  • If you work on your rest day, you must get another rest day in the week before or after, and can never work more than ten days in a row without rest Wages Rules rule 6(2).
  • Work on your rest day is paid at the overtime rate Wages Rules rule 6(4).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: Am I entitled to an experience or service certificate?
answers.rendered:
• Under the model standing orders, you get a service certificate showing your work, designation and period of employment within ten days of leaving order 13(1)(ii).
  • A contractor must give contract labour an experience certificate on demand OSH s. 56.
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.

answers.question: Am I paid while suspended?
answers.rendered:
• You are paid a subsistence allowance of fifty per cent of your wages for the first ninety days s. 38(3)(a).
  • For the rest of the suspension it rises to seventy-five per cent, unless the delay is directly caused by your own conduct s. 38(3)(b).

answers.question: Are apprentices workers, and what are their hours and leave?
also: does labour law apply to apprentices
answers.rendered:
• A person training in a designated trade is a trainee, not a worker, and other labour laws do not apply, except as the Act provides Apprentices Act s. 18.
  • Hours are set by the employer, subject to any prescribed training duration s. 15(1). Overtime needs the Apprenticeship Adviser’s approval s. 15(2), and you get the leave and holidays observed in the establishment s. 15(3).
  • Your employer is liable to pay compensation for an injury in the course of your training s. 16.
notes: This comes from the Apprentices Act, 1961, as amended up to 2014, not the Labour Codes. Its rules, which set the stipend rates, are not in this library.

answers.question: Are domestic workers and farm workers covered?
also: driver or cook at home rights
answers.rendered:
• The minimum wage applies to every employee, whatever the job CW s. 5.
  • An employer of not more than five persons for agriculture or domestic purposes need not keep wage registers, notices or slips, but must show reasonable proof of payment when asked CW s. 50(4).
  • A home-based or other wage worker in the unorganised sector can register for the welfare schemes SS s. 2(86) SS s. 113(1).

answers.question: Are drivers and bus staff covered?
answers.rendered:
• A motor transport worker is a person employed in a motor transport undertaking to work on a transport vehicle, including a driver, conductor and cleaner OSH s. 2(1)(zo).
  • Their hours include running time, subsidiary work and short periods of attendance at terminals OSH s. 25(1), second proviso.

answers.question: Are medical representatives and sales staff covered?
answers.rendered:
• Sales promotion employees are included in the OSH Code’s definition of worker, unless a listed exclusion applies OSH s. 2(1)(zzl).
  • They have separate earned and medical leave rules OSH s. 25(3).

answers.question: Are the old labour Acts still in force?
also: which acts did the codes replace
answers.rendered:
• The Code on Wages repeals the Payment of Wages Act, the Minimum Wages Act, the Payment of Bonus Act and the Equal Remuneration Act s. 69(1).
  • The Industrial Relations Code repeals the Trade Unions Act, the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act and the Industrial Disputes Act s. 104(1).
  • The Code on Social Security and the OSH Code repeal Acts including the EPF, ESI, Maternity Benefit, Gratuity, Factories, Mines and Contract Labour Acts SS s. 164(1) OSH s. 143(1).

answers.question: Are wages and the minimum wage the same thing?
also: difference between wages and minimum wages
does my salary meet minimum wage if allowances count
answers.rendered:
• No. Wages are defined by what you are paid: basic pay, dearness allowance and any retaining allowance, with the 50% rule s. 2(y).
  • The minimum wage is the lowest rate the Government has notified, which your employer cannot pay below s. 5.

answers.question: At what age can a child work?
answers.rendered:
• A child is a person who has not completed their fourteenth year of age, or the age set in the Right to Education Act if that is higher s. 2. No child can be employed or permitted to work in any occupation or process s. 3(1).
  • The exceptions are helping a family or family enterprise in non-hazardous work outside school hours, and work as an artist in audio-visual entertainment or sports, other than the circus s. 3(2).
  • Employing a child can bring imprisonment of six months to two years, a fine of ₹20,000 to ₹50,000, or both s. 14(1).
notes: This comes from the Child and Adolescent Labour Act, 1986, not the Labour Codes. Its official copy is a scan, and we checked the cited pages by eye: see the official copy.

answers.question: By when must bonus be paid?
answers.rendered:
• Bonus must be paid into your bank account within eight months of the close of the accounting year s. 39(1).
  • The Government or an authority it specifies may extend this for sufficient reasons, but never beyond two years in total s. 39(1), proviso.

answers.question: Can a contractor charge me a fee or commission?
answers.rendered: • No. A contractor cannot charge you any fee or commission s. 49.

answers.question: Can a woman be paid less than a man for the same work?
also: lower salary because i am a woman
answers.rendered:
• No. You must not be paid less because of your gender than someone of another gender doing the same or similar work for the same employer s. 3(1).
  • Your employer cannot fix a difference by cutting anyone’s pay s. 3(2)(i).

ministry.label: FAQs on the Code on Wages, 24 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: The Employers shall not discriminate on ground of gender including transgender in matter relating to wages, recruitment of an employee for the same work or work of a similar nature and in the conditions of employment.

answers.question: Can an employer refuse to hire someone because of their sex?
also: recruitment on the ground of sex
answers.rendered:
• An employer cannot discriminate on the ground of sex when recruiting for the same or similar work, or in conditions of employment s. 3(2)(ii).
  • The only exception is work in which the law prohibits or restricts the employment of women s. 3(2)(ii).

ministry.label: FAQs on the Code on Wages, 24 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: The Employers shall not discriminate on ground of gender including transgender in matter relating to wages, recruitment of an employee for the same work or work of a similar nature and in the conditions of employment.

answers.question: Can contract labour be used in core activities?
answers.rendered:
• Employing contract labour in core activities is prohibited, except in the cases the Code lists s. 57(1).
  • A core activity is any activity the establishment is set up for, and anything essential to it s. 2(1)(p).
  • Unless the establishment is set up for them, sanitation, watch and ward, canteen, loading and unloading, housekeeping and similar work are not core s. 2(1)(p).
  • It is allowed if the work is ordinarily done through contractors, does not need full-time workers for most of the day, or is a sudden increase in work to be finished in a specified time s. 57(1), proviso.

answers.question: Can details of a sexual harassment complaint be made public?
also: sharing harassment complaint on social media
answers.rendered: • The complaint, the identities and addresses of the people involved, the proceedings and the action taken must not be made known to the public, press or media s. 16.
notes: This comes from the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, not the Labour Codes. Rules made under it may add detail, and this library does not hold them.

answers.question: Can I be dismissed for misconduct without an inquiry?
also: terminated for misconduct what are my rights
can i be represented in an enquiry
answers.rendered:
• Under the model standing orders, you can appear in person at the enquiry, or be represented by a union office-bearer or a co-worker of your choice order 24(6)(c).
  • A penalty follows only if you are found guilty, and after you have had a reasonable chance to respond to the penalty proposed order 24(6)(f).
  • Dismissing a worker in utter disregard of natural justice in the enquiry is an unfair labour practice Second Schedule.
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 23) and mining (order 24).

answers.question: Can I be given hard work while pregnant?
also: ask for lighter work during pregnancy
answers.rendered:
• If you ask, your employer must not give you hard work, work with long hours of standing, or work that could harm your pregnancy, in the month before the six weeks preceding your expected delivery, or in any part of those six weeks you are still working s. 59(3)–(4).
  • Your normal daily wages cannot be cut because you were given lighter work s. 69.

answers.question: Can I be made to work 12 hours a day for a four-day week?
also: is a twelve hour working day allowed
answers.rendered:
• You cannot be required or allowed to work more than eight hours in a day OSH s. 25(1)(a).
  • Hours beyond that are overtime, which needs your consent and is paid at twice your rate of wages OSH s. 27.

ministry.label: FAQs on the OSH Code, 19 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: The Code prescribes 8 hours per day and 48 hours per week as standard, with some flexibility to extend daily hours with the consent of workers on payment of overtime, at twice the rate wages.
ministry.note: The question spoke of up to twelve hours a day. That figure is not in the Code or the Central Rules.

answers.question: Can I carry forward or encash unused leave?
also: encash my leave when i leave
answers.rendered:
• Up to thirty days of unused leave can be carried forward to the next year s. 32(1)(vii)(a).
  • Leave you applied for and were refused carries forward without any limit s. 32(1)(vii)(b).
  • You may ask to be paid for your leave at the end of the calendar year s. 32(1)(viii).
  • When you leave a job, you are paid for the leave you had earned s. 32(1)(vi).

ministry.label: FAQs on Labour Codes, 30 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: leave encashment is not a part of allowances.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: There is no prescribed maximum limit for leave encashment under the OSH&WC Code, 2020.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: At the time of separation from service, the worker is entitled to encash the leave to his/ her credit.

answers.question: Can I take a second job or do side work?
also: part time job along with full time job
answers.rendered:
• Under the model standing orders, you cannot take up additional work that may adversely affect your employer’s interest order 21(2).
  • Your employer may permit it, with or without conditions, and you must get that permission first order 21(3).
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 20) and mining (order 21).

answers.question: Can many workers file one wage claim together?
answers.rendered:
• A single application can cover many employees of the same establishment s. 45(5).
  • A registered trade union you belong to can file it for you s. 45(4)(b).

answers.question: Can my employer keep my original certificates?
also: employer not returning my original documents
can hr keep my original marksheets
answers.rendered:
• The Labour Codes, the Central Rules and the model standing orders do not deal with an employer keeping a worker’s original certificates or documents.
  • Check your appointment letter. If documents are not returned, the Labour Codes do not set the rules for getting them back.

answers.question: Can my employer refuse to accept my resignation?
also: resignation not accepted what to do
answers.rendered:
• The Labour Codes, the Central Rules and the model standing orders do not deal with an employer accepting or refusing a worker’s resignation.
  • The notice you give usually comes from your appointment letter or your employer’s standing orders. Your final wages still have a deadline under the Codes.

links.label: When your final pay is due

answers.question: Can my salary be paid in cash?
answers.rendered:
• Wages must be paid in coin or notes, by cheque, by credit to your bank account, or electronically s. 15.
  • The Government may require certain establishments to pay only by cheque or bank credit s. 15.

answers.question: Can union fees be deducted from my wages?
answers.rendered: • Only with your written authorisation s. 18(2)(k).

answers.question: Can women work in dangerous or hazardous jobs?
also: women in mines or dangerous factories
answers.rendered:
• Women are entitled to be employed in all establishments for all types of work s. 43.
  • Where the Government considers the work dangerous for their health and safety, it may require the employer to provide adequate safeguards first s. 44.

answers.question: Can women work night shifts?
also: can a woman be forced to work at night
answers.rendered:
• Women are entitled to be employed in all establishments for all types of work s. 43.
  • They may be employed before 6 a.m. and beyond 7 p.m. only with their consent, and subject to conditions on safety, holidays and working hours s. 43.

answers.question: Do apprentices get paid, and how much?
answers.rendered:
• Your employer must pay a stipend at not less than the prescribed minimum rate, as your contract of apprenticeship says Apprentices Act s. 13(1).
  • You cannot be paid by piece work, or required to join an output bonus or incentive scheme Apprentices Act s. 13(2).
notes: This comes from the Apprentices Act, 1961, as amended up to 2014, not the Labour Codes. Its rules, which set the stipend rates, are not in this library.

answers.question: Do Central Rules or my State's Rules apply to me?
also: which rules apply in my state
answers.rendered:
• That depends on your appropriate Government. It is the Central Government for railways, mines, oil fields, major ports, air transport, telecommunication, banking and insurance companies and central public sector undertakings, and the State Government for any other establishment CW s. 2(d).
  • That Government makes the rules that fill in the detail of each Code s. 67(1).

answers.question: Do contract workers get the same pay and conditions as regular workers?
answers.rendered:
• Your wages must be at least the rates under the Code on Wages, or higher rates under an agreement, settlement or award rule 93(1).
  • If you do the same or similar work as the principal employer’s own workers, you get the same holidays, hours of work and other conditions of service rule 93(2).
  • You should be enrolled in provident fund and ESI where those apply rule 93(4).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: Do fixed-term employees get gratuity?
also: contract employee gratuity after one year
fixed term gratuity less than five years
answers.rendered:
• Yes. You do not need five years when a fixed-term contract ends s. 53(1), second proviso.
  • Under the Central Rules, you qualify after at least a year of service under the contract rule 33(1)(a).
  • Gratuity is paid on a pro rata basis s. 53(2), third proviso.
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Fixed Term Employee (FTE) will be eligible for gratuity if he/she renders service under the contract for a period of one year (from start of contract).

answers.question: Do I get gratuity if I resign before five years?
also: four years and seven months gratuity
do i lose gratuity if i resign early
answers.rendered:
• A permanent employee who resigns needs at least five years of continuous service s. 53(1).
  • The five years are not needed on death, disablement or the end of a fixed-term contract s. 53(1), second proviso.
  • If you actually worked at least 240 days in a twelve-month period, that year counts as continuous service s. 54(B).

answers.question: Do I get marriage leave?
answers.rendered:
• The Labour Codes, the Central Rules and the model standing orders do not provide a separate marriage leave.
  • Leave for this comes from your employer’s leave policy or your appointment letter, or from the paid leave you have.

links.label: How much paid leave you get

answers.question: Do I get national and festival holidays?
answers.rendered:
• The Codes do not fix a list of national or festival holidays. Under the model standing orders, a list of them must be displayed order 5(2).
  • Other holidays follow the law, contract, custom and usage that apply to you order 11(1). State laws may set them.
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 5, order 10) and mining (order 5, order 10).

answers.question: Do I get nursing breaks after returning from maternity leave?
answers.rendered:
• You get two nursing breaks a day, on top of your normal rest interval, until your child is fifteen months old s. 66.
  • Each break is 15 minutes, plus up to 15 minutes to get to and from the crèche rule 36(1).
  • Your normal daily wages cannot be cut because of nursing breaks s. 69.
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: Do I get statutory bonus if my salary is above the limit?
also: not eligible for bonus high salary
answers.rendered:
• The statutory bonus is for employees whose wages do not exceed the limit set by the Government s. 26(1).
  • The Central Government’s limit is ₹21,000 a month S.O. 4711(E). A State Government may set its own for employers under it s. 26(1).

answers.question: Do I need to register my establishment?
answers.rendered:
• A new establishment under the OSH Code applies electronically to the registering officer within sixty days of the Code applying to it OSH s. 3(1).
  • A later application can be accepted on payment of late fees OSH s. 3(1), proviso.

links.label: Which duties apply to your workplace

answers.question: Do managers and supervisors get overtime?
answers.rendered:
• The OSH Code’s hours and overtime rules are for workers. A person employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity, or a supervisor drawing wages above ₹18,000 a month, is not a worker s. 2(1)(zzl).
  • Where a minimum rate is fixed for an employee, the Code on Wages requires overtime at not less than twice the normal rate CW s. 14.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Employee, including worker, whose minimum rate of wages is fixed under the Code on Wages, 2019 is eligible for overtime.

answers.question: Do maternity leave, lay-off and holidays count towards the 180 days for leave?
also: joined in the middle of the year leave
answers.rendered:
• Time on lay-off, maternity leave or annual leave counts towards your one hundred and eighty days, though you do not earn leave for that time s. 32(1)(iii).
  • Holidays that fall during your leave do not count as leave used s. 32(1)(iv).
  • If you started work after the first day of January, you earn leave at the same rate once you have worked one-fourth of the remaining days of the year s. 32(1)(v).

answers.question: Do old rules and orders still apply after the Codes?
also: notification under repealed act still valid
answers.rendered:
• Rules, notifications and orders made under the repealed Acts stay in force to the extent they are not contrary to the Code IR s. 104(2).
  • Tribunals and authorities under the repealed Acts continue until those under the Code become functional IR s. 104(1A).

ministry.label: FAQs on Labour Codes, 30 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: As per the provisions of Section 6 of General Clauses Act, 1897, old rules will remain in force till final notification of new rules under the Code, to the extent these are in line with Codes.

answers.question: Do overtime and commission count as wages?
answers.rendered:
• Overtime allowance and commission are left out of wages s. 2(y)(h)–(i).
  • They still count towards the 50% test s. 2(y), first proviso.
  • For equal pay and for paying wages, overtime allowance is counted as wages s. 2(y), second proviso.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Overtime allowance payment forms a part of the 50 percent wage calculation.

answers.question: Do small employers of domestic or farm workers need wage registers?
answers.rendered:
• An employer of not more than five persons for agriculture or domestic purposes need not keep these registers, notices or slips s. 50(4).
  • But they must show reasonable proof of payment to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator when asked s. 50(4).

answers.question: Do the Labour Codes cover apprentices and interns?
answers.rendered:
• An apprentice under the Apprentices Act is left out of the definition of employee CW s. 2(k) IR s. 2(l).
  • The Codes do not use the word intern, so whether you are an employee depends on whether you are employed on wages to do the work the definition lists CW s. 2(k).
  • An apprentice has separate rules under the Apprentices Act, as a trainee and not a worker Apprentices Act s. 18.
notes: This comes from the Apprentices Act, 1961, as amended up to 2014, not the Labour Codes. Its rules, which set the stipend rates, are not in this library.

answers.question: Do the Labour Codes decide income tax on my salary or gratuity?
answers.rendered: • No. Income tax is under a separate law, which this library does not hold. The Code on Wages only allows your employer to deduct income tax from your wages s. 18(2)(h).

answers.question: Do the wage payment rules apply to Government establishments?
also: does payment of wages apply to government
answers.rendered: • The payment rules apply to private employers. They apply to Government establishments only if the Government extends them by notification s. 25.

answers.question: Does a contractor need a licence?
answers.rendered:
• A covered contractor needs a licence before supplying or engaging contract labour s. 47(1).
  • It is valid for five years, for the number of contract labour it states s. 48(3).
  • Under the Central Rules, the security is a bank guarantee at ₹1,000 for each contract labour rule 90(1).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: Does a Diwali or festival bonus count against my statutory bonus?
answers.rendered: • Yes. A customary bonus, such as a puja bonus, or bonus paid in advance during the year can be deducted from the bonus due s. 37.

answers.question: Does a new business have to pay bonus?
answers.rendered: • In the first five accounting years after you begin selling goods or rendering services from a new establishment, bonus is payable only for a year in which you make a profit from it s. 26(6).

answers.question: Does minimum wage apply if I am paid by the piece?
answers.rendered:
• Rates can be fixed for piece work as well as time work s. 6(2).
  • If you are paid by the piece and a minimum time rate applies, you must get at least that time rate s. 12.

answers.question: Does my employer have to pay for a yearly health check?
answers.rendered:
• Your employer must provide a free annual health examination or test to the employees the appropriate Government prescribes OSH s. 6(1)(c).
  • You cannot be charged for medical examinations done to detect occupational diseases OSH s. 6(1)(g).
  • Under the Central Rules, an employer of dock work, building or other construction work arranges a free medical examination for an employee who has completed forty years of age rule 5(1).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

ministry.label: FAQ on the OSH Code, 13 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Free of cost pre-employment and periodic health examinations, irrespective of the age of the worker, would be arranged by the employer for workers employed in factories carrying out hazardous processes and dangerous operations.

answers.question: Does pay given in kind count as wages?
also: food or goods instead of salary
answers.rendered: • If part of your pay is given in kind instead of money, its value counts as wages up to fifteen per cent of your total wages s. 2(y), Explanation.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Benefits under the terms of employment such as food coupons, ration items, mobile recharge etc. would constitute remuneration in kind.

answers.question: Does the law cover me if I am a temporary or part-time employee?
also: am i covered by labour codes
does the code on wages apply to temporary staff
is a white collar employee covered
answers.rendered:
• The Code on Wages covers any person employed on wages by an establishment to do skilled, semi-skilled, unskilled, manual, operational, supervisory, managerial, administrative, technical or clerical work. It does not leave out temporary or part-time staff s. 2(k).
  • An apprentice under the Apprentices Act is not an employee under this definition s. 2(k).
  • Minimum wages apply to every employee, whatever the job s. 5.
  • Other rights have their own limits. Annual leave, for example, is for workers who have worked enough days in the year OSH s. 32(1).

ministry.label: FAQs on the Code on Wages, 24 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: The concept of scheduled employment has been done away under the Code on Wages. The Code is now universally applicable to all employees, irrespective of their sector or category.

answers.question: Does the law give me a right to work from home?
answers.rendered:
• There is no general right. Under the model standing orders for the service sector, your employer may allow it, subject to your conditions of appointment or an agreement order 9.
  • After maternity leave, your employer may let you work from home if your work allows it and you both agree SS s. 60(5).
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.

answers.question: Does the OSH Code apply to Government offices?
answers.rendered:
• It does not apply to offices of the Central or State Government OSH s. 1(3).
  • It does apply to contract labour employed through a contractor in those offices, where that Government is the principal employer OSH s. 1(3), proviso.

answers.question: Does the Shops and Establishments Act still apply?
also: state shops act hours and leave
answers.rendered: • Shops and establishments Acts are State laws. They are not among the Acts the Codes list for repeal, and this library does not hold them. The OSH Code’s list of repealed Acts is in s. 143(1).

answers.question: How and when do I tell my employer about maternity leave?
answers.rendered:
• Give written notice, in Form-XI or on plain paper. Not giving notice does not take away your benefit rule 35(2)(a) s. 62(6).
  • Your employer must pay the part before delivery in advance on proof of pregnancy, and the rest within forty-eight hours of proof of delivery s. 62(5).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: How are PF claims and corrections handled?
also: how long does a pf claim take
where do i complain about pf problems
answers.rendered:
• A complete claim must be settled within twenty days G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 54.
  • Tell the Commissioner about any error in your statement within three months of it being published G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 30.
  • An Authorised Officer can decide what your employer owes, up to five years after the amount fell due s. 125(1).

answers.question: How can an advance or loan be recovered from my wages?
also: company loan cut from my pay
answers.rendered:
• Recovery of advances and of loans from an approved welfare fund, with interest, is an allowed deduction s. 18(2)(f).
  • An advance given before your job began is recovered from your first full wage period, but an advance for travel expenses is not recovered s. 23(a).
  • All deductions in a wage period, including this deduction, cannot be more than fifty per cent of your wages s. 18(3).

answers.question: How do contract workers raise a grievance?
also: where can contract workers raise a complaint
answers.rendered:
• Raise a grievance about health, working conditions or wages with the principal employer rule 184(1).
  • A committee must decide it within thirty days rule 184(3).
  • If not settled, it goes to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator, who must resolve it within sixty days rule 184(4)–(5).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: How do deductions for absence work?
also: salary cut for leave without pay
loss of pay for absent days
can my pay be cut for days i was absent
answers.rendered:
• Your employer can deduct for absence from duty s. 18(2)(b).
  • The cut cannot be a bigger share of your pay than the time you were absent s. 20(2).
  • If ten or more employees stay away together without notice and without reasonable cause, the deduction may include up to eight days’ wages in place of notice s. 20(2), proviso.

answers.question: How do I claim gratuity?
also: how do i apply for gratuity
what can i do if my employer does not pay gratuity
answers.rendered:
• Apply to your employer in Form IV, ordinarily within thirty days of the gratuity becoming due. A late application must still be considered if you give a good reason rule 33(1).
  • Your employer must reply in Form V within fifteen days rule 33(2)(a).
  • If your employer refuses, pays too little or does not reply in time, apply to the competent authority in Form VI within one hundred and eighty days rule 33(4).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: How do I claim wages that are due?
also: where to complain about unpaid salary
company is not paying my salary
file a complaint for salary not paid
what can i do if my employer does not pay my wages
answers.rendered:
• You, a registered trade union you belong to, or an Inspector-cum-Facilitator can file a claim with the authority appointed under the Code s. 45(4).
  • File it within three years of the claim arising; a later claim may be accepted if there is good reason for the delay s. 45(6).
  • The authority can order your employer to pay what is owed plus compensation of up to ten times that amount s. 45(2).

answers.question: How do I complain about sexual harassment at work?
also: my boss harassed me where do i go
answers.rendered:
• Make a written complaint to the Internal Committee, or to the Local Committee if there is no Internal Committee, within three months of the incident, or of the last incident in a series s. 9(1).
  • The Committee can extend that by up to three months if circumstances prevented you, and its members must help you put the complaint in writing if you cannot s. 9(1).
  • If you are unable to complain because of physical or mental incapacity or death, your legal heir or another prescribed person may do so s. 9(2).
notes: This comes from the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, not the Labour Codes. Rules made under it may add detail, and this library does not hold them.

answers.question: How do I convert the minimum wage to an hourly or monthly rate?
answers.rendered:
• Where the Central Government fixes rates, it fixes them by the day rule 3(1).
  • The hourly rate is the daily rate divided by eight, and the monthly rate is the daily rate multiplied by twenty six rule 3(2).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: How do I qualify for a PF pension?
answers.rendered:
• A monthly pension needs at least ten years of eligible service G.S.R. 527(E), paragraph 12(1).
  • With less than that, you get a withdrawal benefit instead G.S.R. 527(E), paragraph 13.
  • Out of your employer’s share, eight and one-third per cent of wages goes to the Pension Fund S.O. 3580(E).

answers.question: How do I raise a safety concern at work?
also: what can i do if my workplace is dangerous
answers.rendered:
• You can get information from your employer about your health and safety at work, and raise inadequate protection with your employer and then the Inspector-cum-Facilitator OSH s. 14(1).
  • If you reasonably fear imminent serious injury, death or danger to health, tell your employer and at the same time the Inspector-cum-Facilitator OSH s. 14(2).
  • If your employer disagrees, the matter goes to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator, whose decision is final OSH s. 14(4).

answers.question: How do we register a trade union?
also: how many members for trade union
answers.rendered:
• Any seven or more members can apply s. 6(1).
  • At least ten per cent of the workers, or one hundred workers, whichever is less, must be members when applying s. 6(2).

answers.question: How does an industrial dispute go to conciliation and the Tribunal?
answers.rendered:
• The conciliation officer cannot hold proceedings more than two years after the dispute arose s. 53(1), proviso.
  • The officer must report within forty-five days of starting, or within fourteen days where there is a strike or lock-out notice s. 53(5).
  • If it is not settled, any party can apply to the Tribunal within ninety days of receiving the report s. 53(6).

answers.question: How is a dispute about the end of a job raised?
also: fired unfairly what can i do
how do i challenge my dismissal
answers.rendered:
• A dispute about your discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination counts as an industrial dispute even if no union or other worker is part of it IR s. 4(9).
  • You can apply to the conciliation officer, and then directly to the Tribunal after forty-five days s. 4(10).
  • That application must be made within two years of the termination s. 4(11).

answers.question: How is bonus calculated if my wages are above the limit?
answers.rendered:
• If your wages are above the calculation limit, bonus is worked out on that limit or on the minimum wage, whichever is higher s. 26(2).
  • The Central Government’s calculation limit is ₹7,000 a month S.O. 4710(E).

answers.question: How is gratuity worked out for piece-rated or seasonal workers?
answers.rendered:
• If you are paid by the piece, your daily wage is the average of what you earned in the last three months, not counting overtime s. 53(2), first proviso.
  • In a seasonal establishment that does not employ you all year, you get 7 days’ wages for each season s. 53(2), second proviso.

answers.question: How is my PF pension amount worked out?
also: how much pension will i get
answers.rendered:
• For a member other than an existing member, monthly pension is pensionable wages multiplied by pensionable service, divided by 70 G.S.R. 527(E), paragraph 12(2).
  • Pensionable wages cannot be more than the wage ceiling for each period, and the pension is worked out pro rata for each ceiling period G.S.R. 527(E), paragraph 12(2), provisos.
  • An existing member’s pension also adds amounts for earlier service G.S.R. 527(E), paragraph 12(3).

answers.question: How is overtime worked out?
answers.rendered:
• If you are paid monthly, your daily wage for overtime is 1/26th of your monthly wage rule 69(3).
  • 15 to 30 minutes of extra work counts as thirty minutes, and more than thirty minutes counts as a full hour rule 69(2).
  • Overtime is paid at twice your rate of wages OSH s. 27.
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: How is salary paid by mistake recovered?
also: company paid me extra and wants it back
can my employer recover salary paid to me by mistake
answers.rendered:
• Adjustment of an overpayment of wages is an allowed deduction s. 18(2)(f)(i).
  • All deductions in a wage period cannot be more than fifty per cent of your wages s. 18(3).

answers.question: How long can a suspension or inquiry last?
answers.rendered:
• The investigation and inquiry should ordinarily be completed within ninety days of your suspension s. 38(1).
  • Under the model standing orders, a statement of the reasons must be given to you within a week order 24(6)(b).
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 23) and mining (order 24).

answers.question: How long can a wage period be?
also: can salary be paid every two months
answers.rendered: • A wage period can be a day, a week, a fortnight or a month, and can never be longer than a month s. 16.

answers.question: How long can probation last?
answers.rendered:
• Under the model standing orders, a probationer is provisionally employed to fill a permanent vacancy and has not completed six months’ service in it order 2(5).
  • The period may be extended by up to three months after an assessment of performance order 2(5), proviso.
  • A worker who satisfactorily completes the probationary period is a permanent worker order 2(2).
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 2) and mining (order 2).

answers.question: How long do I have to claim accident compensation?
also: late claim for accident at work
answers.rendered:
• Give notice of the accident as soon as practicable, and claim within two years of the accident, or of the date of death s. 82(1).
  • If your employer is more than a month late in paying, the competent authority shall direct interest, and may add up to fifty per cent of the arrears as damages if there is no justification for the delay s. 77(3).

answers.question: How long is paid maternity leave?
also: am i eligible for maternity leave
answers.rendered:
• You can be paid for up to twenty-six weeks, of which not more than eight weeks can be before your expected delivery s. 60(3).
  • If you have two or more surviving children, the limit is twelve weeks, of which not more than six can be before your expected delivery s. 60(3), first proviso.
  • You must have actually worked for your employer for at least eighty days in the twelve months before your expected delivery s. 60(2).
  • Your employer cannot dismiss you during, or because of, this absence s. 68(1).

answers.question: How many contract workers bring in the contract labour rules?
answers.rendered:
• The rules apply where fifty or more contract labour work in the establishment, or to a manpower supply contractor with fifty or more, counting any day of the preceding twelve months s. 45(1).
  • They do not apply where only intermittent or casual work is done s. 45(2).

answers.question: How many hours can I be made to work?
also: maximum working hours in a week
how long can my employer make me work
answers.rendered:
• You cannot be made to work more than eight hours in a day OSH s. 25(1)(a).
  • Under the Central Rules, your week cannot be more than forty-eight hours rule 64(1).
  • You cannot work more than six days in a week OSH s. 26(1).
  • Work beyond these hours is overtime, which needs your consent and is paid at twice your rate of wages OSH s. 27.
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

ministry.label: FAQs on the OSH Code, 19 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: The Code prescribes 8 hours per day and 48 hours per week as standard, with some flexibility to extend daily hours with the consent of workers on payment of overtime, at twice the rate wages.
ministry.note: The question spoke of up to twelve hours a day. That figure is not in the Code or the Central Rules.

answers.question: How much am I paid during a lay-off?
answers.rendered:
• With at least a year of continuous service, you are paid fifty per cent of your basic wages and dearness allowance for the days you are laid off, apart from weekly holidays s. 67.
  • This applies to factories, mines and plantations with fifty or more workers, below the size that needs Government permission, and not to seasonal or intermittent work s. 65(1).
  • You lose it if you refuse suitable other work within eight kilometres at your normal wages, or do not present yourself at least once a day s. 69.

answers.question: How much am I paid while on annual leave?
answers.rendered:
• The Code gives leave “with wages” OSH s. 32(1). I found no separate formula for workers in the Code or the Central Rules, so check your employer’s terms and your State’s rules.
  • Working journalists and sales promotion employees have their own leave rules OSH s. 25(3).

answers.question: How much compensation is paid for death or disablement at work?
also: family of worker who died in accident
answers.rendered:
• For death, it is fifty per cent of monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor for the employee’s age, or the notified amount if that is more s. 76(1)(a).
  • For permanent total disablement, it is sixty per cent of monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor, or the notified amount if that is more s. 76(1)(b).
  • It must be paid as soon as it falls due s. 77(1).

answers.question: How much ESI is paid?
answers.rendered:
• Your employer pays three and one-fourth per cent of the wages payable to you rule 19(1)(a).
  • You pay three-fourth per cent rule 19(1)(b).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: How much gratuity will I get?
also: how much money is my gratuity
answers.rendered:
• You get 15 days’ wages at the rate last drawn for every completed year of service, and a part year of more than six months counts as a full year s. 53(2).
  • If you are paid monthly, a day’s wages is your monthly wage divided by 26 s. 53, Explanation 3.
  • Your employer must pay within 30 days of it becoming payable, or pay interest for the delay s. 56(3)–(4).
notes: The Labour Ministry's FAQs give the limit as ₹20,00,000, from S.O. 1420(E) under the old Payment of Gratuity Act. See the note in the gratuity guide.

answers.question: How much is overtime pay?
also: am i paid correctly for overtime
answers.rendered:
• Overtime is paid at twice your rate of wages, and you can be asked to work overtime only if you agree OSH s. 27.
  • It is worked out by the day or by the week, whichever is better for you OSH s. 27.
  • Under the Central Rules, overtime begins after eight hours in a day for a daily wager, or after forty-eight hours in a week for other workers, and is paid at the end of each wage period rule 69(1).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: How much leave is given after a miscarriage?
answers.rendered:
• Six weeks after a miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy s. 65(1).
  • Two weeks after a tubectomy operation s. 65(2).
  • Up to a month more if you fall ill because of pregnancy, delivery, premature birth, miscarriage or termination s. 65(3).

answers.question: How much maternity pay will I get?
answers.rendered:
• You are paid your average daily wage for each day you are actually away s. 60(1).
  • That is the average of what you were paid for the days you worked in the three calendar months before your leave, and it cannot be less than the minimum wage s. 60(1), Explanation.

answers.question: How much must an aggregator contribute for gig workers?
answers.rendered:
• The rate is notified by the Central Government, at not more than two per cent of annual turnover s. 114(4).
  • It cannot be more than five per cent of what the aggregator pays gig and platform workers s. 114(4), proviso.
  • The start date is to be notified by the Central Government s. 114(5).

answers.question: How much notice is needed before a strike?
answers.rendered:
• A strike needs notice to the employer within the sixty days before striking, and cannot start within fourteen days of the notice s. 62(1)(a)–(b).
  • A strike is also barred during conciliation proceedings and for seven days after them s. 62(1)(d).
  • Under the Central Rules, notice is given in Form-XI rule 25(1).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

ministry.label: Myths and Realities of the IR Code, 23 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: No permission is required from the Government under the IR Code. However, 14-Days prior strike notice will be required

answers.question: How much notice must I give when I resign?
also: can i leave without serving notice
answers.rendered: • The Codes set no single notice period for resigning, so check your appointment letter. Resigning does not take away your final wages, which are due within two working days CW s. 17(2).

answers.question: How much notice must my employer give to end my job?
answers.rendered:
• Under the model standing orders, a permanent worker gets a month’s notice or wages instead order 23(1)(i).
  • A temporary worker, probationer, substitute, or fixed-term or casual worker whose contract is not renewed or has expired gets no notice or pay instead order 23(2).
  • Retrenchment has its own notice rule s. 70(a).
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 22) and mining (order 23).

answers.question: How much overtime can I be asked to work?
also: can my boss force me to work overtime
answers.rendered:
• You can be asked to work overtime only if you agree OSH s. 27.
  • Under the Central Rules, overtime cannot be more than one hundred forty-four hours in any quarter of a year rule 69(4), proviso.
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: How much paid leave do I get in a year?
answers.rendered:
• If you work one hundred and eighty days or more in a calendar year, you get paid annual leave s. 32(1)(i).
  • You earn one day of leave for every twenty days you work s. 32(1)(ii).
  • This covers workers. A person employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity, or a supervisor drawing wages above ₹18,000 a month, is not a worker s. 2(1)(zzl).

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Leave provisions apply to workers as per the OSH & WC Code, 2020 and only to those supervisors having wage not exceeding Rs 18,000/ per month.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: However, an employee is entitled to benefits under State Law if more favourable to him than those under the Code.

answers.question: How much provident fund (PF) is paid each month?
also: how much pf is cut from salary
answers.rendered:
• In most covered establishments, you and your employer each pay twelve per cent of wages S.O. 3582(E).
  • If your wages are above ₹25,000 a month, the contribution is normally worked out on ₹25,000 S.O. 5109(E) G.S.R. 703(E).
  • Your employer cannot make you pay its share G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 21.
  • Your employer must send the money within fifteen days of the close of each month G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 28.
  • Provident fund applies to establishments with twenty or more employees First Schedule.

answers.question: How much retrenchment compensation will I get?
also: compensation for being laid off permanently
answers.rendered:
• You get fifteen days’ average pay for every completed year of continuous service, and a part year of more than six months counts s. 70(b).
  • If you are paid monthly, average pay is the average of your wages in the last three complete calendar months s. 2(d).
  • Your employer must also put fifteen days of your last wages into the worker re-skilling fund, which credits it to you within forty-five days s. 83(2)(a) s. 83(3).

answers.question: How much sick leave or casual leave do I get?
also: fell ill and have no leave
how many sick leaves in a year
answers.rendered:
• The Codes do not use the words sick leave. If you are insured under ESI, sickness benefit is paid on a medical certificate SS s. 32(1)(a).
  • Under the model standing orders, you may be granted casual leave with wages of up to ten days in a calendar year order 12(1).
  • Casual leave is not for more than three days at a time, except for sickness and unforeseen circumstances order 12(1), proviso.
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 11) and mining (order 12).

answers.question: How must I apply for leave, and can it be refused?
also: reasons for refusing leave in writing
answers.rendered:
• Under the model standing orders, leave cannot be claimed as a matter of right order 11(2).
  • You apply at least seven days in advance order 11(3).
  • If leave is refused or postponed, you must be told in writing with the reasons order 11(6).
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 10) and mining (order 10).

answers.question: How often is the minimum wage changed?
also: cost of living allowance april october
answers.rendered:
• Rates are to be reviewed ordinarily at intervals of not more than five years s. 8(4).
  • Where the Central Government fixes rates, the cost of living allowance is revised before 1 April and again before 1 October every year rule 4.
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: How often must I get a break at work?
answers.rendered:
• Where the Central Government is the appropriate Government, you cannot be made to work more than five hours at a stretch without a break of at least half an hour S.O. 2517(E).
  • Your State Government notifies this where it is the appropriate Government OSH s. 25(1)(b).

answers.question: How soon must I get my last pay after leaving a job?
also: full and final settlement time limit
when will i get my final salary after resigning
two days rule for final wages
when do i get my money after resigning
answers.rendered:
• Your wages must be paid within two working days of your resignation, dismissal or retrenchment, or of the workplace closing s. 17(2).
  • Wages for earned annual leave you did not take must be paid before the second working day after you leave s. 32(1)(vi)(a).
  • If you retire, those leave wages must be paid within two months s. 32(1)(vi)(b).

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: At the time of separation from service, the worker is entitled to encash the leave to his/ her credit.

answers.question: I am a daily wager and got less than a full day's work. Must I be paid for the full day?
also: less than a normal working day
answers.rendered: • If you are on a daily rate and your employer gives you less than a full day’s work, you must still be paid for the full day, unless you chose not to work s. 10.

answers.question: I did not work the whole year. Do I still get bonus?
also: left the job before bonus paid
answers.rendered:
• You qualify if you worked at least thirty days in the accounting year s. 26(1).
  • If you did not work all the working days, the minimum bonus can be reduced in proportion s. 27.
  • Days on lay-off, paid leave, maternity leave with wages, or off work after an accident at work count as days you worked s. 28.

answers.question: I do two kinds of work with different minimum wages. Which rate applies?
also: more than one type of work wage
answers.rendered: • You must get at least the right rate for the time you spend on each kind of work s. 11.

answers.question: Is an employment bond or non-compete clause valid?
answers.rendered: • The Codes and Central Rules do not set rules on employment bonds or non-compete clauses, so this library cannot answer it. Your contract and other laws decide it. Standing orders only say a worker cannot act against the establishment’s interest while employed order 21(1).
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 20) and mining (order 21).

answers.question: Is bonus payable if the company made a loss?
also: company says no bonus this year
answers.rendered: • Yes. The minimum bonus is payable whether or not there is an allocable surplus s. 26(1).

answers.question: Is compensation paid for a disease caught at work?
answers.rendered:
• Your employer must pay compensation for an occupational disease listed in the Third Schedule that arises out of and in the course of your work SS s. 74(1).
  • A doctor attending you must report a listed disease without delay OSH s. 12(2).

answers.question: Is gratuity for my service before the Codes worked out on the new wages?
also: does the new wage definition apply to past years
answers.rendered: • Gratuity is based on the rate of wages you last drew, for every completed year of service s. 53(2).

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Gratuity, based on revised definition of wages will be applicable w.e.f. 21.11.2025 i.e. date of implementation of the Codes.

answers.question: Is house rent allowance (HRA) part of wages?
also: does hra count for pf or gratuity
answers.rendered:
• House rent allowance is left out of wages s. 2(y)(f).
  • But if the left-out payments together come to more than half of your total pay, the part above half is added to wages s. 2(y), first proviso.
  • For equal pay and for paying wages, house rent allowance is counted as wages s. 2(y), second proviso.

answers.question: Is maternity leave available for adoption or surrogacy?
answers.rendered: • If you legally adopt a child below the age of three months, or you are a commissioning mother, you get twelve weeks from the day the child is handed to you s. 60(4).

answers.question: Is my CTC the same as my wages?
also: what is left out of wages
answers.rendered:
• No. Wages mean basic pay, dearness allowance and any retaining allowance, plus any excess under the 50% rule s. 2(y).
  • Your employer’s contribution to provident fund or pension is left out s. 2(y)(c).
  • Gratuity, retrenchment compensation and other payments when your job ends are left out too s. 2(y)(j)–(k).

ministry.label: FAQs on Labour Codes, 30 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: Performance based incentives, Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOPs), variable part of the component or reimbursement-based payments to the employee shall not be part of the wages.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Annual performance-based incentives do not form a part of “wages” for computation under the Labour Codes.

answers.question: Is the end of a fixed-term contract retrenchment?
answers.rendered:
• No. The end of a fixed-term employment, or a contract not being renewed, is not retrenchment s. 2(zh)(iii)–(iv).
  • Under the model standing orders, no notice or pay instead is due when the contract expires or is not renewed order 23(2).
  • You do not need five years for gratuity SS s. 53(1), second proviso.
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 22) and mining (order 23).

answers.question: Is there a helpline for migrant workers?
also: help number for workers from other states
answers.rendered: • The Government may provide a toll free helpline for inter-State migrant workers OSH s. 63. The Code does not say it must.

ministry.label: FAQs on the OSH Code, 19 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: The Code requires setting up of Toll free helpline number for Inter State Migrant Worker (ISMW).
ministry.note: Section 63 says the appropriate Government may provide this helpline. The Code prevails.

answers.question: Is there bereavement leave when a family member dies?
also: leave when a family member dies
leave after my father passed away
answers.rendered:
• The Labour Codes, the Central Rules and the model standing orders do not provide a separate bereavement leave.
  • Leave for this comes from your employer’s leave policy or your appointment letter, or from the paid leave you have.

links.label: How much paid leave you get

answers.question: Is there life insurance with PF?
answers.rendered:
• Your employer pays for this and cannot take it from your wages G.S.R. 526(E), paragraph 8.
  • If you die in service after a continuous twelve months in employment, the amount for your family is at least ₹2,50,000. It depends on your wages and your account balance G.S.R. 526(E), paragraph 21.

answers.question: Is there menstrual leave under the Labour Codes?
answers.rendered:
• The Labour Codes, the Central Rules and the model standing orders do not provide for menstrual leave.
  • Some employers give it under their own leave policy, so check your appointment letter or the leave policy where you work.

answers.question: Is there paternity leave under the Labour Codes?
answers.rendered: • The Codes and the Central Rules do not provide paternity leave, though your employer’s own policy may. Annual leave with wages is available to covered workers s. 32(1).

answers.question: Must I join PF if my wage is above the ceiling?
answers.rendered:
• If your wage is above ₹25,000 a month when you would otherwise join, you need not be a member G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 2 S.O. 5109(E).
  • You and your employer may jointly choose in writing to enrol you G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 9.

answers.question: Must my employer give me a job after apprenticeship, and where do I raise a dispute?
answers.rendered:
• Every employer makes its own policy on recruiting apprentices who finish training s. 22(1). If your contract requires you to serve after training, the employer must offer suitable employment s. 22(2).
  • A dispute arising from the contract goes to the Apprenticeship Adviser, and you can appeal within thirty days s. 20(1)–(2).
notes: This comes from the Apprentices Act, 1961, as amended up to 2014, not the Labour Codes. Its rules, which set the stipend rates, are not in this library.

answers.question: Must my employer give me a yearly salary increase?
answers.rendered:
• The Codes do not require a yearly increase. Minimum rates are reviewed ordinarily at intervals of not more than five years, and your pay cannot fall below them s. 8(4) s. 5.
  • Your contract, a settlement or an award may give you more. Withholding an increment for good cause is not treated as a deduction, where the conditions are met s. 18(1), Explanation.

answers.question: Must my employer give me an appointment letter?
also: what must an appointment letter say
answers.rendered:
• Yes. An employer must issue a letter of appointment to every employee on appointment OSH s. 6(1)(f).
  • An employee without a letter before the Code began must get it within three months of the Code starting OSH s. 6(1)(f).
  • Under the Central Rules, it shows your designation, type of employment, skill category, date of joining, wages and allowances, and social security benefits rule 6.
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: Must my old employer offer me my job back if it hires again?
answers.rendered: • If your employer hires within a year of retrenching you, you must be offered the chance to come back, ahead of others s. 72.

answers.question: What am I owed if my workplace closes down?
answers.rendered:
• With at least a year of continuous service, you get notice and compensation as if you had been retrenched s. 75(1).
  • If the closure is due to unavoidable circumstances beyond the employer’s control, compensation is capped at three months’ average pay. Financial losses and unsold stock do not count as such circumstances s. 75(1), proviso and Explanation.
  • Your wages are due within two working days CW s. 17(2).

answers.question: What am I paid if I am off work for a while after an accident?
answers.rendered:
• You get a half-monthly payment of twenty-five per cent of your monthly wages SS s. 76(1)(d).
  • It is paid during the disablement, or for five years, whichever is shorter SS s. 76(4).

answers.question: What are a principal employer's duties for contract labour?
answers.rendered:
• Provide the Code’s welfare facilities to the contract labour in your establishment s. 53.
  • Use only licensed contractors s. 54.
  • If the contractor has not paid within seven days of the end of the wage period, pay the labour within fifteen days and recover it from the contractor rule 98(8).
  • Set up a grievance committee for health, working conditions and wages rule 184(1)–(2).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

ministry.label: FAQ on the OSH Code, 13 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: It is the responsibility of the principal employer under Section-53 to provide the welfare facilities prescribed under Section-23 & 24 to the contract labours.

answers.question: What are my duties as an employer under the Labour Codes?
answers.rendered:
• The checklist linked below shows the duties your headcount and sector bring in. The annual return in Form XVII must reach the Inspector-cum-Facilitator electronically on or before the last day of February following each calendar year OSH rule 74.
  • A new establishment under the OSH Code applies for registration within sixty days of the Code applying to it OSH s. 3(1).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

links.label: Which duties apply to your workplace

answers.question: What are my own safety duties as an employee?
answers.rendered:
• Take reasonable care for your own health and safety and that of others affected by what you do OSH s. 13(a).
  • Comply with the safety and health standards, and co-operate with your employer in meeting its duties under the Code OSH s. 13(b)–(c).
  • Report any unsafe or unhealthy situation to your employer as soon as practicable OSH s. 13(d).

answers.question: What are standing orders and who needs them?
answers.rendered:
• They are the written rules on conditions of service, such as classification, hours, leave, termination and misconduct First Schedule.
  • They are needed in an industrial establishment with three hundred or more workers, now or on any day of the preceding twelve months s. 28(1).
  • Until your own are certified, the Model Standing Orders are treated as adopted s. 29(2).

answers.question: What are the Labour Codes?
answers.rendered: • They are the Code on Wages s. 1(1), the Industrial Relations Code s. 1(1), the Code on Social Security s. 1(1) and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code s. 1(1).

answers.question: What are the penalties under the Labour Codes?
answers.rendered:
• Under the Code on Wages, paying less than is due can bring a fine of up to ₹50,000, and other contraventions up to ₹20,000 CW s. 54(1).
  • Under the OSH Code, a contravention with no other penalty stated carries a penalty of ₹2,00,000 to ₹3,00,000 OSH s. 94.
  • Under the OSH Code, the Inspector-cum-Facilitator must first give thirty days to comply, except in the cases that section lists OSH s. 110(1).

links.label: Which duties apply to your workplace

answers.question: What are the PF payment deadlines and late charges?
also: what happens if an employer pays pf late
answers.rendered:
• Pay within fifteen days of the close of each month G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 28.
  • Simple interest runs at twelve per cent a year from the date the amount fell due S.O. 2698(E).
  • Damages may also be levied, up to the amount of the arrears G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 23.
  • Late returns carry a fee of ₹500 a day, up to the administrative charges for that month G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 29.

answers.question: What are the rules for night shifts?
answers.rendered:
• If your shift goes past midnight, your weekly holiday is twenty-four hours in a row starting when your shift ends, and the hours after midnight count towards the day your shift began OSH s. 28.
  • You cannot be made to work in a factory or mine if you worked in another similar workplace in the previous twelve hours OSH s. 30.

answers.question: What are the rules on a lock-out?
answers.rendered:
• An employer must give notice within the sixty days before a lock-out, and cannot start it within fourteen days of the notice s. 62(2)(a)–(b).
  • A lock-out in breach of these rules is illegal s. 63(1).

answers.question: What are the rules on deductions for damage or loss?
also: company made me pay for damage
cash shortage cut from my wages
can my employer charge me for something i damaged or lost
answers.rendered:
• A deduction is allowed for damage or loss directly caused by your own neglect or default s. 18(2)(c).
  • It cannot be more than the actual loss, and you must be given a chance to explain first s. 21(1)–(2).
  • Your employer must record the deduction in a register s. 21(3).

answers.question: What are the rules on deductions for housing, amenities and tools?
also: charged for equipment needed for job
can my employer deduct money for tools, housing or canteen food
answers.rendered:
• A deduction for housing, amenities or services is allowed only if you accepted them and it is no more than their value s. 22.
  • “Services” here does not include the supply of tools and raw materials needed for the job s. 18(2)(e), Explanation.

answers.question: What are the rules on late attendance?
also: can my pay be cut for coming late
answers.rendered:
• Under the model standing orders, a worker attending late is liable to deduction of wages as the Code on Wages provides order 10(1).
  • Attendance is kept by identity card, biometrics or another notified system order 10(4).
  • A deduction for absence cannot be a bigger share of your pay than the time you were absent CW s. 20(2).
  • Habitual late attendance is on the list of misconduct order 24(5)(d).
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 9, order 23) and mining (order 9, order 24).

answers.question: What are the working limits for 14 to 18 year olds?
also: can a 17 year old work at night
answers.rendered:
• An adolescent has completed their fourteenth year of age but not their eighteenth year s. 2, and cannot work in mines, with inflammable substances or explosives, or in hazardous processes s. 3A.
  • A period of work cannot be more than three hours before a rest of at least one hour s. 7(2), spread over no more than six hours including rest s. 7(3).
  • No work between 7 p.m. and 8 a.m., and no overtime s. 7(4)–(5). A whole day’s holiday every week s. 8.
notes: This comes from the Child and Adolescent Labour Act, 1986, not the Labour Codes. Its official copy is a scan, and we checked the cited pages by eye: see the official copy.

answers.question: What benefits does ESI give?
also: what do i get from esic
answers.rendered:
• Sickness benefit, maternity benefit, disablement benefit and dependants’ benefit, as periodical payments s. 32(1)(a)–(d).
  • Medical treatment for and attendance on insured persons s. 32(1)(e).
  • Funeral expenses for an insured person who has died s. 32(1)(f).

answers.question: What can the authority order on a wage claim?
also: how long does a wage claim take
employer ignores order to pay wages
answers.rendered:
• It can order what you are owed plus compensation of up to ten times that amount, and should try to decide within three months s. 45(2).
  • If your employer still does not pay, the authority sends a recovery certificate to the Collector or District Magistrate, who recovers it as arrears of land revenue s. 45(3).

answers.question: What compensation is there for an injury at work?
also: who pays when a worker is injured at work
who pays if i am hurt in an accident at work
answers.rendered:
• Your employer must pay compensation for personal injury from an accident arising out of and in the course of your work s. 74(1).
  • It is not payable for an injury that disables you for three days or less s. 74(1)(a).
  • Unless the result is death or permanent total disablement, it is not payable if the accident was directly caused by your being under the influence of drink or drugs, or wilfully disobeying a safety rule or removing a safety guard s. 74(1)(b).

answers.question: What counts as a factory?
answers.rendered: • Premises with twenty or more workers where a manufacturing process runs with power, or forty or more without power, counting any day of the preceding twelve months OSH s. 2(1)(w).

answers.question: What counts as continuous service for gratuity?
answers.rendered:
• Time off for sickness, an accident, leave, a lay-off, a strike or a lock-out does not break your continuous service s. 54(A).
  • A year also counts if you actually worked at least 240 days in the twelve months, or 190 days if you work below ground in a mine or your workplace works fewer than six days a week s. 54(B).

answers.question: What counts as misconduct?
also: can i be fired for being late
answers.rendered:
• The model standing orders list, among others, theft, fraud, wilful disobedience, habitual lateness or absence, drunkenness, fighting, sleeping on duty and sexual harassment order 24(5).
  • Continuous absence without permission and without satisfactory cause for more than ten days is on the list order 24(5)(l).
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 23) and mining (order 24).

answers.question: What counts as sexual harassment at work?
also: what does the law say about sexual harassment
answers.rendered:
• It includes unwelcome physical contact and advances, a demand or request for sexual favours, sexually coloured remarks, showing pornography, and other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature s. 2(n).
  • No woman shall be subjected to it at any workplace s. 3(1).
  • The model standing orders treat it as misconduct order 24(5)(x), and an employee convicted of it is not entitled to bonus CW s. 29.
notes: This comes from the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, not the Labour Codes. Rules made under it may add detail, and this library does not hold them.

The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 23) and mining (order 24).

answers.question: What counts as the same or similar work?
also: is my job similar for equal pay
answers.rendered:
• Work is the same or similar when it needs the same skill, effort, experience and responsibility, under similar working conditions s. 2(v).
  • Small differences between jobs do not count unless they matter in practice to the terms and conditions of employment s. 2(v).

answers.question: What counts as wages under the new law?
also: which parts of my salary are wages
answers.rendered:
• Wages include basic pay, dearness allowance and any retaining allowance s. 2(y).
  • Some payments are left out, such as house rent allowance, conveyance allowance, overtime allowance and commission s. 2(y).
  • If those left-out payments together come to more than half of your total pay, the excess is added to wages s. 2(y), first proviso.
  • For equal pay and for paying wages, house rent allowance, conveyance allowance and overtime allowance are counted as wages anyway s. 2(y), second proviso.

ministry.label: FAQs on Labour Codes, 30 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: Performance based incentives, Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOPs), variable part of the component or reimbursement-based payments to the employee shall not be part of the wages.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Annual performance-based incentives do not form a part of “wages” for computation under the Labour Codes.

ministry.label: FAQs on Labour Codes, 30 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: This single definition of wages applies across all four Labour Codes

answers.question: What do the Codes say about transfers?
also: can my employer transfer me to punish me
answers.rendered:
• Transferring a worker mala fide, under the guise of following management policy, is an unfair labour practice IR Second Schedule.
  • Unfair labour practices are prohibited IR s. 84. The Codes do not otherwise set general transfer rules, so check your appointment letter.

answers.question: What does an Inspector-cum-Facilitator do?
also: who do i complain to at the labour department
answers.rendered:
• Inspector-cum-Facilitators advise employers and workers on complying with the Code, and inspect the establishments assigned to them s. 51(5).
  • Your workplace notice must show the name and address of the Inspector-cum-Facilitator s. 50(2).

answers.question: What does the law give unorganised workers?
answers.rendered:
• An unorganised worker is a home-based worker, self-employed worker or wage worker in the unorganised sector s. 2(86).
  • The Central Government frames welfare schemes on life and disability cover, health and maternity benefits and old age protection s. 109(1).
  • State Governments frame schemes including provident fund, employment injury benefit, housing and funeral assistance s. 109(2).

answers.question: What does the law say for transgender employees?
answers.rendered:
• Bathing places and locker rooms must be separate for male, female and transgender employees OSH s. 24(1)(ii).
  • Rules may require separate shelters or rest rooms for them too OSH s. 24(2)(iii).
  • Employers cannot discriminate on the ground of gender in wages for the same or similar work CW s. 3(1).

ministry.label: FAQs on the Code on Wages, 24 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: The Employers shall not discriminate on ground of gender including transgender in matter relating to wages, recruitment of an employee for the same work or work of a similar nature and in the conditions of employment.

answers.question: What employee numbers bring in each law?
also: how many employees before pf esi gratuity
what applies to a company of 25 people
answers.rendered:
• Ten or more workers make a place an establishment under the OSH Code OSH s. 2(1)(v).
  • ESI starts at ten persons, provident fund at twenty employees, and gratuity at ten employees for shops and establishments First Schedule.
  • Bonus starts at twenty persons CW s. 41(2), and standing orders at three hundred workers IR s. 28(1).

links.label: Which duties apply to your workplace

answers.question: What happens after a sexual harassment complaint?
answers.rendered:
• The inquiry must be completed within ninety days s. 11(4). The report goes to the employer within ten days of that s. 13(1).
  • During the inquiry you can ask in writing for a transfer of you or the other person, or up to three months’ extra leave s. 12(1).
  • If the complaint is proved, the Committee can recommend action for misconduct and a sum to be paid to you from the person’s wages s. 13(3). The employer must act within sixty days s. 13(4).
