  • An appeal must be made within ninety days of the recommendations s. 18(2).
notes: This comes from the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, not the Labour Codes. Rules made under it may add detail, and this library does not hold them.

answers.question: What happens if a sexual harassment complaint is false?
answers.rendered:
• If the Committee concludes a complaint is malicious or knowingly false, it may recommend action against the person who made it s. 14(1).
  • Merely being unable to prove a complaint is not enough for action s. 14(1), proviso.
notes: This comes from the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, not the Labour Codes. Rules made under it may add detail, and this library does not hold them.

answers.question: What happens if a strike is illegal?
answers.rendered:
• A strike started in breach of the notice and other rules is illegal s. 63(1).
  • Taking part in an illegal strike can bring a fine of ₹1,000 to ₹10,000, imprisonment of up to a month, or both s. 86(13).
  • Concerted casual leave on a given day by fifty per cent or more of workers counts as a strike s. 2(zk).

answers.question: What happens to leave my employer refused?
answers.rendered:
• If you asked for leave and were refused, that leave carries forward with no limit s. 32(1)(vii)(b).
  • Ask your employer for your leave record: they must keep it in Form XX and share it with you once a calendar year if you ask rule 76(1).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: What happens to my job if the business is sold?
answers.rendered:
• With at least a year of continuous service, you are entitled to notice and compensation as if retrenched s. 73.
  • That does not apply if your service is not interrupted, your terms are no less favourable and the new employer is liable for compensation based on your full service s. 73, proviso.

answers.question: What happens to my PF when I change jobs?
answers.rendered: • You can apply on the portal to move your balance to your new job’s account G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 43.

answers.question: What if my employer did not insure me or pay my ESI?
answers.rendered:
• If that leaves you without a benefit, or on a lower scale, the Corporation may pay you the benefit you would have had, and recover the value from your employer s. 42(1).
  • Not paying a contribution is an offence s. 133(a).

answers.question: What is a Grievance Redressal Committee?
answers.rendered:
• Every industrial establishment with twenty or more workers must have one, for disputes from individual grievances IR s. 4(1).
  • An aggrieved worker can apply within one year of the cause s. 4(5), and the Committee may finish within thirty days s. 4(6).
  • If you disagree or it is not resolved in that time, you can apply through your Trade Union for conciliation within sixty days s. 4(8).

answers.question: What is a lay-off?
also: laid off because of power cut or machine breakdown
answers.rendered:
• A lay-off is when an employer fails, refuses or cannot give work to a worker on the muster roll because of a shortage of coal, power or raw materials, accumulated stock, machinery breakdown, natural calamity or a connected reason s. 2(t).
  • A worker who is laid off has not been retrenched s. 2(t).

answers.question: What is an unfair labour practice?
answers.rendered:
• These include threatening dismissal for joining a union, dismissing by way of victimisation, and keeping workers as casuals or temporaries for years to deny them the status of permanent workers Second Schedule.
  • They are prohibited s. 84, and can bring a fine of ₹10,000 to ₹2,00,000 s. 86(5).

answers.question: What is the 50% rule for wages?
also: basic pay at least half of salary
how does the 50 per cent rule work
answers.rendered:
• If the payments left out of wages are more than half of your total pay, the part above half is added to wages s. 2(y), first proviso.
  • Gratuity and payments when your job ends are not part of this test s. 2(y), first proviso.
  • The Code on Social Security has the same rule for its own definition of wages s. 2(88).

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Only statutory components such as employer PF and pension contributions and statutory bonus are included for arriving at 50% of wages to form part of remuneration. Gratuity, ESI and other retirement benefits are not included.
ministry.note: The Ministry's earlier worked example (FAQ 7 of 30 December 2025) counted gratuity and retrenchment compensation in total remuneration. This later reply does not, and the calculator follows it.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Overtime allowance payment forms a part of the 50 percent wage calculation.

answers.question: What is the actual minimum wage rate in my State?
also: how much is minimum wage for unskilled worker
answers.rendered:
• This library does not list the rates. They are fixed by notification s. 5, for each skill level and area s. 6(6), and change often, so check the latest notification from your State’s labour department.
  • Depending on your workplace, the Central Government or your State Government fixes your rate s. 2(d).

answers.question: What is the cess for building and construction workers?
answers.rendered:
• A cess of not more than two per cent of the cost of construction is collected from employers for the social security and welfare of building workers, at the rate the Central Government notifies SS s. 100(1).
  • The cost of land is not counted SS s. 100(1), Explanation.

answers.question: What is the difference between an employee and a worker?
also: am i a worker or an employee
answers.rendered:
• An employee is anyone employed on wages to do skilled, unskilled, manual, operational, supervisory, managerial, administrative, technical or clerical work, other than an apprentice and the Armed Forces CW s. 2(k).
  • A worker is narrower. Under the OSH Code, a person employed mainly as a manager or administrator is not a worker, nor is a supervisor drawing wages above eighteen thousand rupees a month OSH s. 2(1)(zzl).

answers.question: What is the floor wage?
answers.rendered:
• The floor wage is fixed by the Central Government, based on minimum living standards, and may differ by area s. 9(1).
  • No minimum rate can be lower than the floor wage, and a rate already above it cannot be reduced s. 9(2).

answers.question: What is the least my employer can pay me?
also: is my pay below the minimum wage
employer pays less than minimum wages
answers.rendered:
• Your employer must pay you at least the minimum rate of wages notified by the Government s. 5.
  • Depending on your workplace, that is the Central Government or your State Government s. 2(d).
  • The rate depends on your skill level, on where you work, or on both s. 6(6).
  • No minimum rate can be below the floor wage set by the Central Government s. 9(2).

ministry.label: FAQs on the Code on Wages, 24 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: The concept of scheduled employment has been done away under the Code on Wages. The Code is now universally applicable to all employees, irrespective of their sector or category.

answers.question: What is the limit on deductions from wages?
also: can my company cut my pay
employer deducted money from my wages
what can be cut from salary
how much of my pay can be taken
how much can my employer deduct from my salary
answers.rendered:
• All deductions together cannot be more than fifty per cent of your wages for the wage period s. 18(3).
  • Your employer can deduct only for reasons the Code allows, such as fines, absence, loss caused by your own neglect, advances and loans, taxes and provident fund s. 18(2).
  • For damage or loss, the cut cannot be more than the actual loss, and you must be allowed to explain first s. 21(1)–(2).

answers.question: What is the maternity medical bonus?
answers.rendered: • You get a medical bonus of ₹3,500, or a higher amount if notified, unless your employer gives you free care before and after the birth s. 64.

answers.question: What is the maximum gratuity I can get?
also: is there a cap on gratuity
answers.rendered:
• Gratuity cannot be more than the amount the Central Government notifies s. 53(3).
  • If your contract or an agreement gives you a better gratuity, you keep the better terms s. 53(5).
notes: The Labour Ministry's FAQs give the limit as ₹20,00,000, from S.O. 1420(E) under the old Payment of Gratuity Act. See the note in the gratuity guide.

answers.question: What is the most bonus I can get?
answers.rendered:
• Where the allocable surplus is larger, bonus rises in proportion to wages, up to twenty per cent of wages s. 26(3).
  • A productivity or production bonus can be agreed, but total bonus cannot be more than twenty per cent of wages s. 26(5).

answers.question: What is the penalty for paying less than the minimum wage?
also: employer pays below minimum wage punishment
answers.rendered:
• Paying less than the Code requires can bring a fine of up to ₹50,000 s. 54(1)(a).
  • A repeat within five years can bring imprisonment of up to three months, a fine of up to ₹1 lakh, or both s. 54(1)(b).

answers.question: What is the penalty for retrenching workers illegally?
also: employer punished for layoff without notice
answers.rendered:
• Breaking the rules on retrenchment, lay-off compensation, transfer or closure compensation can bring a fine of ₹50,000 to ₹2,00,000 s. 86(3).
  • Breaking the rules that need Government permission can bring a fine of ₹1,00,000 to ₹10,00,000 s. 86(1).

answers.question: What is the PF wage ceiling?
answers.rendered:
• The wage ceiling is ₹25,000 a month S.O. 5109(E).
  • If your wages are above that, the contribution is normally worked out on ₹25,000 S.O. 5109(E) G.S.R. 703(E).
  • You may choose to pay more on wages above that, and your employer need not match it G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 19.

answers.question: What is the retirement age?
answers.rendered:
• Under the model standing orders, it is the age agreed in writing, or set by a settlement or award order 16(1).
  • If no age is agreed, it is fifty-eight years order 16(2).
notes: The model standing orders are for industrial establishments with three hundred or more workers (IR Code s. 28(1)), and your employer's certified standing orders may differ. Elsewhere, check your appointment letter, and see what applies at a smaller workplace.
The citations are to the service sector's model. These points read the same for manufacturing (order 15) and mining (order 16).

answers.question: What is the time limit for a wage claim?
also: can i claim old salary dues
how long do i have to claim unpaid wages
answers.rendered:
• You can file within three years of the claim arising s. 45(6).
  • The authority can accept a later claim if you show good reason for the delay s. 45(6), proviso.

answers.question: What is the wage limit for ESI?
also: salary above which esi does not apply
answers.rendered:
• The wage ceiling for becoming a member under the ESI Chapter is the amount the Central Government notifies s. 2(89).
  • The ₹25,000 ceiling is for the provident fund Chapter only S.O. 5109(E).

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: At present, Rs 21,000 per month wages notified for ESI coverage will be applicable.
ministry.note: This library has not found a notification of this figure under the Code.

answers.question: What is the worker re-skilling fund?
answers.rendered:
• For every retrenched worker, the employer contributes fifteen days’ wages last drawn s. 83(2)(a).
  • The fund credits that amount to the worker within forty-five days of the retrenchment s. 83(3).
  • Under the Central Rules, the employer transfers it electronically within ten days of the retrenchment rule 37(1), (3).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: What job protection is there during pregnancy and maternity leave?
also: what can i do if i am dismissed during pregnancy or maternity leave
answers.rendered:
• Your employer cannot dismiss you during, or because of, your maternity absence s. 68(1).
  • Being dismissed while pregnant does not take away the benefit you would otherwise have received s. 68(1), first proviso.
  • If you are not paid or are dismissed because of your absence, complain to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator s. 72(1), who must decide within 45 days rule 39(1)(b).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: What must an employer do after an accident at work?
answers.rendered:
• Give notice of an accident that causes death, or an injury that keeps the person from working for forty-eight hours or more OSH s. 10(1).
  • Under the Central Rules, a death must be reported forthwith in Form-XI to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator rule 7(1).
  • An injury must be reported in Form-XI within twelve hours after the forty-eight hours are completed rule 7(2).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: What must an employer do under the sexual harassment law?
answers.rendered:
• Provide a safe working environment, display the penal consequences and the order setting up the Internal Committee, and run awareness workshops s. 19(a)–(c).
  • Treat sexual harassment as misconduct and act on it s. 19(i).
  • Include the number of cases and their disposal in your annual report s. 22.
  • Failing to set up the Committee or to act can bring a fine of up to fifty thousand rupees s. 26(1).
notes: This comes from the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, not the Labour Codes. Rules made under it may add detail, and this library does not hold them.

answers.question: What must an employer do when gratuity becomes payable?
answers.rendered:
• Work out the amount and notify the employee and the competent authority in writing, even if no application has been made s. 56(2).
  • Pay within thirty days of the date it becomes payable s. 56(3), or pay simple interest for the delay s. 56(4).
  • If the amount is disputed, deposit the amount you admit with the competent authority s. 56(5)(a).

answers.question: What must an employer provide for women on night shifts?
answers.rendered:
• Under the Central Rules, take the woman’s consent in writing and provide transport to pick her up and drop her at her residence rule 83(a), (c).
  • Keep the workplace and the passage to toilets, washrooms and drinking water well lit, with suitable closed-circuit television on the way to those facilities rule 83(d).
  • Display dedicated telephone numbers at the establishment and inside vehicles rule 83(f).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: What must be displayed on the notice board about wages?
answers.rendered: • A notice must show an abstract of the Code, the wage rates for each category, the wage period, the day or date and time of payment, and the name and address of the Inspector-cum-Facilitator s. 50(2).

answers.question: What must my employer do to keep the workplace safe?
answers.rendered:
• Your employer must keep the workplace free from hazards that cause or are likely to cause injury or occupational disease OSH s. 6(1)(a).
  • Your employer cannot charge you for anything done or provided for safety and health at work OSH s. 6(1)(g).

answers.question: What notice is needed to change pay, hours or shifts?
also: notice of change in service conditions
can my employer change my pay, hours or shifts without notice
answers.rendered:
• An employer proposing to change listed conditions must give notice to the workers affected, and cannot make the change within twenty-one days of that notice IR s. 40.
  • The list includes wages, allowances, hours of work, rest intervals, leave with wages and holidays Third Schedule.

answers.question: What notice is needed when an employer ends a job?
also: can my employer remove me without notice
answers.rendered:
• When an employer ends your job for a reason other than punishment, that is generally retrenchment. Retirement, the end of a fixed-term contract and continued ill-health are not s. 2(zh).
  • After at least a year of continuous service, you must get a month’s written notice giving the reasons, or wages for that period instead s. 70(a).
  • You must also be paid fifteen days’ average pay for every completed year, counting more than six months as a year s. 70(b).
  • A factory, mine or plantation with at least three hundred workers needs the Government’s prior permission, and must give three months’ notice or wages s. 77(1) s. 79(1).
  • These rules protect workers. A person employed mainly as a manager or administrator, or a supervisor drawing wages above ₹18,000 a month, is not a worker s. 2(zr).

ministry.label: Compliance Handbook for Employers, Feb 2026
ministry.quote: Industrial establishments such as factories, mines, and plantations employing 50 to 299 workers must serve notice on appropriate government or such authority as specified by the appropriate government before carrying out any lay-off, retrenchment, or closure.
ministry.note: Section 70's retrenchment conditions have no such range: they cover a worker employed in any industry with a year's continuous service. The Code prevails.

answers.question: What notice must an employer give before closing down?
answers.rendered:
• Give the appropriate Government at least sixty days’ notice of an intended closure, with reasons s. 74(1).
  • That notice is not needed for an establishment with less than fifty workers on every day of the preceding twelve months, or an establishment set up for construction work s. 74(1), proviso.
  • The larger factories, mines and plantations must apply for permission at least ninety days before closing s. 80(1).

answers.question: What notice of working hours must be displayed?
answers.rendered:
• Display and keep up to date a notice of periods of work, showing clearly for every day when workers may be required to work OSH s. 31(1).
  • Tell the Inspector-cum-Facilitator before changing the system of work OSH s. 31(3).

answers.question: What protection do workers have while a dispute is pending?
also: can i be punished while my dispute is pending
answers.rendered:
• While a dispute is pending, your employer cannot alter your conditions on any matter connected with it to your prejudice, or discharge or punish you for misconduct connected with it, without written permission from the authority IR s. 90(1).
  • You can complain in writing to that authority IR s. 91.

answers.question: What rights do fixed-term employees have?
also: fixed term equal pay to permanent
employment on a contract for a fixed period
answers.rendered:
• Fixed term employment is engagement on a written contract for a fixed period IR s. 2(o).
  • Your hours, wages, allowances and other benefits cannot be less than those of a permanent worker doing the same or similar work s. 2(o), proviso (a).
  • You get all statutory benefits proportionately, even if your period does not reach the qualifying period s. 2(o), proviso (b).

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Fixed Term Employment covers employees directly engaged by the employer.

answers.question: What rights do inter-State migrant workers have?
answers.rendered:
• You are an inter-State migrant worker if you work in a State other than where you were recruited or came from, and draw wages of not more than eighteen thousand rupees a month or a higher notified amount s. 2(1)(zf).
  • These rules apply where ten or more inter-State migrant workers are employed s. 59.
  • Once a year your employer pays a lump sum fare for the journey to your native place and back s. 61.

ministry.label: FAQs on the OSH Code, 19 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: The Code requires setting up of Toll free helpline number for Inter State Migrant Worker (ISMW).
ministry.note: Section 63 says the appropriate Government may provide this helpline. The Code prevails.

answers.question: What rules apply at a workplace with fewer than 300 workers?
also: small company leave and notice rules
no standing orders in my company
my company has 50 people which rules apply
answers.rendered:
• Standing orders are required at three hundred or more workers, so a smaller workplace need not have them IR s. 28(1).
  • The Codes still apply to you: wages CW s. 5, an appointment letter OSH s. 6(1)(f), and the grievance committee at twenty or more workers IR s. 4(1).
  • Notice, probation, casual leave and retirement age then come from your appointment letter and any State law. Retrenchment has its own rule at any size IR s. 70.

answers.question: What social security do gig workers get?
answers.rendered:
• The Central Government may frame schemes on life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity benefits, old age protection and crèches s. 114(1).
  • To use a scheme you must be registered, which needs you to be at least sixteen years of age and to give a self-declaration s. 113(1), (3).

answers.question: What special leave and fine rules apply to teenage workers?
answers.rendered:
• You earn a day of annual leave for every fifteen days of work OSH s. 32(1)(ii).
  • Nobody under fifteen years of age can be fined CW s. 19(5).
  • Your hours follow the Child and Adolescent Labour Act OSH s. 25(4).

answers.question: What special rules apply to mine workers?
answers.rendered:
• If you work below ground in a mine, a shift cannot be more than eight hours in a day S.O. 2516(E).
  • You earn a day of annual leave for every fifteen days of work OSH s. 32(1)(ii).
  • For gratuity, 190 days worked in the twelve months counts as a year of continuous service SS s. 54(B).

answers.question: What special rules apply to working journalists?
answers.rendered:
• Your hours cannot be more than one hundred and forty-four in any four consecutive weeks, with at least twenty-four consecutive hours of rest in every seven consecutive days OSH s. 25(2).
  • You need three years, not five, for gratuity SS s. 53(1), first proviso.
  • You have separate earned and medical leave rules OSH s. 25(3).

answers.question: What wage records must an employer keep?
answers.rendered:
• Keep a register of the persons employed, the muster roll and wages s. 50(1).
  • Under the Central Rules, these can be kept electronically or on paper, in the Forms the Rules set out rule 51(1).
  • Failing to maintain records, or maintaining them improperly, can bring a fine of up to ₹10,000 s. 54(2).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: What welfare facilities must a workplace have?
also: must a workplace have a canteen
answers.rendered:
• Separate washing facilities, separate bathing places and locker rooms, and first-aid boxes OSH s. 24(1).
  • A canteen where one hundred or more workers, including contract labourers, are ordinarily employed OSH s. 24(1)(v).
  • Rules may require shelters, rest rooms and a lunch room in a factory or mine with more than fifty workers, and an ambulance room in a factory, mine or building work with more than five hundred OSH s. 24(2)(i), (iii).

answers.question: When can a fine be taken from wages?
also: company charged a penalty from my pay
answers.rendered:
• You can be fined only for acts listed in an approved notice displayed at your workplace, and only after you have been allowed to explain s. 19(1)–(3).
  • Fines in one pay period cannot be more than three per cent of your wages for that period s. 19(4).
  • A fine cannot be taken in instalments, or more than ninety days after it was imposed s. 19(6).
  • Nobody under fifteen years of age can be fined s. 19(5).

answers.question: When can gratuity be reduced or withheld?
also: can my employer refuse to pay gratuity after dismissal
answers.rendered:
• If you were dismissed for damaging your employer’s property on purpose or through negligence, the employer can deduct the loss from your gratuity s. 53(6)(a).
  • If you were dismissed for riotous or disorderly conduct or violence, or for an offence involving moral turpitude committed in the course of your work, it can be withheld in part or in full s. 53(6)(b).

answers.question: When can I lose my bonus?
answers.rendered:
• You lose it if you are dismissed for fraud, violent or riotous behaviour at work, theft, misappropriation or sabotage, or are convicted of sexual harassment s. 29.
  • If you are found guilty of misconduct causing financial loss, the loss can be deducted from that year’s bonus only s. 38.

answers.question: When can I withdraw my provident fund?
answers.rendered:
• After twelve months as a member, you can apply to take out money for illness, education or marriage, for yourself or your family, or for a home G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 46.
  • Twenty-five per cent of your contributions, including your employer’s share and interest, must stay in the account G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 46.
  • You can withdraw everything if you retire after the age of fifty-five, or if you lose your job through retrenchment G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 49.
  • In other cases, you must have been out of covered employment for a continuous twelve months before applying. That wait does not apply to a woman who resigns to get married G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 49.

answers.question: When did the Labour Codes come into force?
also: are the labour codes in force
date the new labour codes started
since when are the codes in force
answers.rendered:
• The Central Government brought most of their provisions into force on 21 November 2025 S.O. 5322(E) S.O. 5320(E) S.O. 5319(E) S.O. 5321(E).
  • Each section’s page in this library shows its own status s. 1(3).

answers.question: When does an employer need Government permission to retrench?
answers.rendered:
• A factory, mine or plantation with not less than three hundred workers on average per working day in the preceding twelve months, or a higher number if notified, needs it s. 77(1), (3).
  • It must also give three months’ notice or wages instead s. 79(1).
  • If the Government does not reply within sixty days of the application, permission is deemed granted s. 79(4).
  • A retrenchment without applying, or after refusal, is illegal, and the workers keep all their benefits s. 79(7).

ministry.label: Myths and Realities of the IR Code, 23 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: Industries having 300 workers on any day of previous year will need prior permission from the Government.
ministry.note: The Code's own test differs: workers employed on an average per working day in the preceding twelve months [s. 77(1)]. The Code prevails.

answers.question: When is a Works Committee required?
answers.rendered: • The Government may require a Works Committee in an industrial establishment with one hundred or more workers, now or on any day of the preceding twelve months s. 3(1).

answers.question: When is the annual return due?
also: returns to file each year as an employer
answers.rendered: • Under the Central Rules, the return in Form XVII must reach the Inspector-cum-Facilitator electronically on or before the last day of February following each calendar year rule 74.
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: When must an employer appoint a safety officer?
answers.rendered:
• In a factory with five hundred workers or more, a factory with a hazardous process or building work with two hundred fifty or more, and a mine with one hundred or more OSH s. 22(2).
  • A factory, mine or plantation with two hundred and fifty or more workers may be required to appoint a welfare officer OSH s. 24(2)(iv).

answers.question: When must an employer provide a crèche?
answers.rendered:
• An establishment with fifty or more employees must provide a crèche for children under the age of six years rule 37(1).
  • It must be within a kilometre of the establishment, or in a common facility in a notified industrial park or area if the competent authority relaxes this rule 37(2)(i).
  • A woman is allowed four visits a day, including her rest intervals s. 67(1), proviso.
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: The creche facility is available to employees, irrespective of gender.

ministry.label: FAQs on the Social Security Code, 9 Jan 2026
ministry.quote: Where crèche facilities are not provided, payment of a crèche allowance is mandated.
ministry.note: Written before the final Rules. Rule 37(2)(viii) ties the allowance to an agreement with the negotiating union or council, or a majority of employees, and names women, widower and single parent employees.

answers.question: When must contract workers be paid?
also: wages through bank for contract labour
answers.rendered:
• Before the end of the seventh day after your wage period rule 98(2), and no wage period can be longer than a month rule 98(1).
  • You should be paid by bank transfer or electronically s. 55(2).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: When must my salary be paid?
also: employer has not paid my salary this month
by what date must wages be paid
answers.rendered:
• If you are paid monthly, wages are due before the end of the seventh day of the next month s. 17(1)(iv).
  • If you are paid by the fortnight, they are due before the end of the second day after the fortnight ends s. 17(1)(iii).
  • If you are paid by the week, they are due on the last working day of the week, before the weekly holiday s. 17(1)(ii).
  • If you are paid by the day, they are due at the end of the shift s. 17(1)(i).

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: The Code on Wages, 2019 has provisions for timely payment of wages. These provisions are applicable to all employees.

answers.question: Which union negotiates with the employer?
answers.rendered:
• A union with fifty-one per cent or more of the workers on the muster roll is the sole negotiating union s. 14(3).
  • If no union has that, the employer sets up a negotiating council of unions that each have at least twenty per cent s. 14(4).

answers.question: Which wages are used to work out gratuity?
also: gratuity on basic or full salary
does the new wage definition raise gratuity
answers.rendered:
• Gratuity is based on the rate of wages you last drew s. 53(2).
  • Wages include basic pay and dearness allowance, and allowances are added back if they are more than half of your total pay s. 2(88).

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Any payment made to employee which is not part of components mentioned under section 2(88) of the Code on Social Security, 2020 shall not be considered for calculation of gratuity.

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: Gratuity, based on revised definition of wages will be applicable w.e.f. 21.11.2025 i.e. date of implementation of the Codes.

answers.question: Which workplaces come under ESI?
also: esi applicable to how many employees
answers.rendered:
• Every establishment with ten or more persons, other than a seasonal factory First Schedule.
  • Every employee in a covered establishment must be insured s. 28(1).

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: At present, Rs 21,000 per month wages notified for ESI coverage will be applicable.
ministry.note: This library has not found a notification of this figure under the Code.

answers.question: Which workplaces do not have to pay bonus?
answers.rendered:
• The bonus rules apply to establishments with twenty or more persons, now or on any day of the accounting year s. 41(2).
  • They do not apply to, among others, the Life Insurance Corporation, the Reserve Bank of India, Government departments and local authorities, universities and other educational institutions, and non-profit hospitals s. 41(1).

answers.question: Which workplaces must give maternity benefit?
also: maternity applicable to how many employees
am i covered for maternity pay
answers.rendered:
• Every factory, mine and plantation, including those belonging to Government First Schedule.
  • Every shop or establishment with ten or more employees, now or on any day of the preceding twelve months First Schedule.

answers.question: Which workplaces must have provident fund?
also: pf applicable to how many employees
answers.rendered:
• Every establishment with twenty or more employees First Schedule.
  • If the employer and most employees agree, the Central Provident Fund Commissioner may apply it to a smaller establishment s. 1(5).

answers.question: Which workplaces must pay gratuity?
also: gratuity applicable to how many employees
answers.rendered:
• Every factory, mine, oilfield, plantation, port and railway company First Schedule.
  • Every shop or establishment with ten or more employees, now or on any day of the preceding twelve months First Schedule.

answers.question: Which workplaces need an Internal Committee?
also: less than ten employees harassment complaint
answers.rendered:
• Every employer of a workplace must set up the Committee by written order, at every office or unit s. 4(1).
  • It has a senior woman employee as Presiding Officer, at least two employee members, and a member from a women’s organisation or a person familiar with these issues s. 4(2).
  • At least half the members must be women s. 4(2).
  • Where there is no Internal Committee because there are fewer than ten workers, or where the complaint is against the employer, the district’s Local Committee takes it s. 6(1).
notes: This comes from the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, not the Labour Codes. Rules made under it may add detail, and this library does not hold them.

answers.question: Who and where does the sexual harassment law protect?
also: does posh cover interns and contract staff
harassment by a client or outside person
answers.rendered:
• It protects a woman of any age, whether employed or not, at a workplace, and a woman employed in a house s. 2(a).
  • Employees include regular, temporary, daily wage and contract workers, probationers, trainees and apprentices, paid or not s. 2(f).
  • A workplace includes private organisations, and any place visited because of the job, including transport from the employer s. 2(o).
notes: This comes from the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, not the Labour Codes. Rules made under it may add detail, and this library does not hold them.

answers.question: Who can certify pregnancy for maternity benefit?
answers.rendered: • A certificate in Form-X from a registered medical practitioner, an Accredited Social Health Activist or a qualified Auxiliary Nurse and Midwife rule 35(1).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: Who can file a complaint in court under the Code on Wages?
also: court case against employer for wages
can i file a criminal complaint against my employer under the code on wages
answers.rendered:
• A court can act on a complaint made by the Government or an officer it authorises, an employee, a registered Trade Union or an Inspector-cum-Facilitator s. 52(1).
  • No court below a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class can try these offences s. 52(2).

answers.question: Who counts as contract labour?
answers.rendered:
• You are contract labour if you are hired by or through a contractor for work in or connected with an establishment, whether or not the principal employer knows of it s. 2(1)(m).
  • It does not include the contractor’s own regular employee on agreed standard conditions, with periodic increments, social security and welfare benefits s. 2(1)(m).

answers.question: Who decides a question about equal pay?
also: employer says my work is different
who decides if work is similar
deputy chief labour commissioner equal pay
where do i complain about unequal pay
answers.rendered:
• If your employer says your work is not the same or similar, the question is decided by the authority the Government has notified s. 4. In the Central sphere, that is the Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) for your area S.O. 2450(E).
  • You, a registered trade union you belong to, or an Inspector-cum-Facilitator can file a claim for wages you were not paid s. 45(4).

answers.question: Who decides the minimum wage for my job?
also: where can i find the minimum wage rate
answers.rendered:
• Your rate is notified by the appropriate Government s. 5.
  • That is the Central Government for its own establishments and for railways, mines, oil fields, major ports, air transport, telecommunication, banking and insurance companies and central public sector undertakings s. 2(d)(i).
  • For any other establishment, it is the State Government s. 2(d)(ii).

answers.question: Who gets a bonus, and how much?
answers.rendered:
• You are eligible if your wages are within the limit set by the Government and you worked at least thirty days in the accounting year s. 26(1).
  • The Central Government’s limit is ₹21,000 a month S.O. 4711(E).
  • The minimum is eight and one-third per cent of wages earned or one hundred rupees, whichever is higher s. 26(1).
  • Bonus must be paid within eight months of the close of the accounting year s. 39(1).
  • The bonus rules apply to workplaces with twenty or more people, or that had that many on any day of the accounting year s. 41(2).

ministry.label: FAQs on the Code on Wages, 24 Dec 2025
ministry.quote: Bonus is payable to every employee who has worked for at least thirty days in an accounting year as per the wage ceiling prescribed by the appropriate government.
ministry.note: The Ministry was asked about daily wage workers.

answers.question: Who gets my gratuity if I die?
answers.rendered:
• Your nominee is paid, or your heirs if you have not made a nomination s. 53(1), third proviso.
  • You make a nomination once you complete a year of service, in favour of your family if you have one s. 55.

answers.question: Who gets my PF if I die?
answers.rendered:
• Make your nomination on the portal, in favour of your family if you have one G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 44.
  • Make a fresh nomination when you marry, because the earlier one stops being valid G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 44.
  • With no valid nomination, the money goes to your family in equal shares G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 50.

answers.question: Who gets the wages of an employee who has died?
also: family claim final salary after death
answers.rendered:
• Amounts payable under the Code are paid to the person the employee nominated s. 44(1)(a).
  • If there is no nomination, or they cannot be paid to the nominee, they are deposited with the authority prescribed s. 44(1)(b).
  • Leave wages are paid to the heir or nominee within two months OSH s. 32(1)(vi)(b).

answers.question: Who is a gig or platform worker?
also: swiggy zomato uber driver labour law
answers.rendered:
• A gig worker earns from work outside a traditional employer-employee relationship s. 2(35).
  • A platform worker does work through an online platform, outside such a relationship, to solve specific problems or provide specific services for payment s. 2(60)–(61).

answers.question: Who is responsible for contract workers' wages?
also: what if my contractor does not pay me
answers.rendered:
• If the contractor pays you late or short, the principal employer must pay you the full amount or the balance s. 55(3).
  • Under the Central Rules, the principal employer must pay within fifteen days rule 98(8).
  • You, your registered trade union or an Inspector-cum-Facilitator can also file a claim under the Code on Wages, within three years s. 45(4), (6).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: Who is responsible for depositing PF deducted from wages?
also: pf cut from salary but not in my account
my employer deducted pf from my pay but did not deposit it. am i responsible
answers.rendered:
• If your employer deducts money for your provident fund or another fund and does not deposit it, you are not responsible for that failure s. 18(5).
  • A sum deducted from your wages counts as money entrusted to your employer to pay your contribution G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 22.
  • Not paying contributions is an offence s. 133.

answers.question: Who is responsible for my wages if my employer fails to pay?
also: company or owner liable for unpaid wages
answers.rendered: • If your employer fails to pay, the company, firm, association or other person who is the proprietor of the establishment is responsible for the payment s. 43, proviso.

answers.question: Who pays gratuity to contract workers?
answers.rendered:
• Gratuity is payable by your employer after at least five years of continuous service s. 53(1).
  • An employee under the Code includes a person employed through a contractor s. 2(26).

ministry.label: Additional FAQs, 16 Mar 2026
ministry.quote: the employer (i.e. Contractor) will pay gratuity on rendering of five years continuous service
ministry.note: The Ministry was asked whether the principal employer or the contractor bears gratuity for contract labour.

answers.question: Who pays PF for workers hired through a contractor?
answers.rendered:
• The principal employer is responsible for paying contributions for employees engaged through a contractor G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 20.
  • The contractor is jointly and severally responsible with the principal employer G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 27.

answers.question: Who pays the employer's share of PF?
also: both pf shares cut from my pay
can my employer take its pf share from my salary
answers.rendered:
• No. Your employer cannot make you pay its share G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 21.
  • Your employer also cannot cut your wages because of its own contribution s. 124.
  • Doing so is an offence s. 133(b).

answers.question: Who should be retrenched first?
answers.rendered:
• Unless there is an agreement, the last person employed in the category goes first, unless the employer records reasons for choosing someone else s. 71.
  • Under the Central Rules, a seniority list must be posted at least seven days before the retrenchment rule 28(1).
notes: Where this uses the Central Rules, your State's Rules may differ: see your State.

answers.question: Who sits on an Industrial Tribunal?
answers.rendered:
• A Tribunal has two members, a Judicial Member and an Administrative Member IR s. 44(2).
  • A bench can be both of them, or a single member of either kind IR s. 44(3).

answers.question: Will I get a chance to fix a breach before being prosecuted under the Code on Wages?
answers.rendered:
• For most breaches other than underpayment, and for records, the Inspector-cum-Facilitator must first give you a written direction and time to comply s. 54(3).
  • Some offences can be compounded on application by a Gazetted Officer, for fifty per cent of the maximum fine s. 56(1).
